chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: George Shearing and Art Tatum
summary: Machito shared two pleasant weeks at Birdland with Shearing, who credited him with his love of Afro-Cuban music.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Sure will. Okay, do you remember when you met George Shearing?

Oh, he is another honey. Well, he - that was his debut in the United States. He came from England and he rehearsed his group and we happened to open the same day, at the Birdland, and as always, clean-playing, beautiful sound, good control, his pedal, good taste and everything and we had a tremendous time. We worked together two weeks. One
of the most pleasant two weeks that I ever spent in my life, like when we was with Art Tatum at the Band Box. He was another pleasant person.
George Shearing told me that the first time he heard you and Afro-Cuban jazz, was at the Club Clique and then he decided to record Afro-Cuban music. That's what he told me.
Yeah, he always said: 'Machito, you know, you get me in trouble, because I fell in love with Afro-Cuban music'.
Yeah, that's why he hired [Armando] Peraza and all those conga players.
